findings.title: [P1] Detach the message listener during cleanup
findings.body: After the returned disposer is called, the `"message"` handler remains registered. Later messages can invoke disposed handlers, while repeated attach/cleanup cycles retain listeners and cause duplicate processing.

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body: The interval handle is discarded and the returned disposer does nothing. Polling therefore continues after teardown, repeated starts accumulate timers, retained closures cannot be collected, and the live timer can prevent Node.js processes or tests from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore removal of the message listener during cleanup
findings.body:
After callers invoke the returned disposer, the handler remains registered. Any later `"message"` event still invokes torn-down state, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and can trigger EventEmitter leak warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body:
Invoking the returned cleanup function no longer stops polling. `refresh` continues after teardown, repeated starts accumulate concurrent pollers, and in Node.js the live interval can prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup no longer revokes the handler. If cleanup marks logout, tenant switching, or socket replacement, an attacker controlling the old socket can continue delivering messages to a handler retaining the previous privileged context.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval in the disposer
findings.body:
Every poller now permanently retains and invokes its callback. In a server that creates and disposes pollers per remotely triggerable session or connection, repeated churn causes unbounded timers, callback execution, and retained state, enabling resource-exhaustion denial of service.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer no longer clears the interval. The callback continues running every second, retained closures cannot be collected, and in Node.js the referenced timer can prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Detach the message listener during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned disposer leaves the handler attached for the socket’s lifetime. Any teardown/remount cycle accumulates retained handlers, causing duplicate processing and unbounded listener/object retention.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
